lessons.correction: Strengthen your ground army, continue teching, and add units that counter the enemy's composition (e.g., Roaches against Zealots/Stalkers).
lessons.mistake: Engaging in a straight-up fight without proper army composition, or over-investing in economy at the expense of defense.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate if the enemy adds air units or changes their composition significantly.
lessons.title: Ground vs Ground: Avoid Straight-Up Fight
lessons.when: Midgame, enemy scouted as ground-heavy with Zealots, Stalkers, Sentries, possibly Immortals; your army is ground-based with Zerglings, Roaches, Queens.
lessons.why: Matching the enemy's ground strength is necessary to hold off potential pushes and maintain map control.

lessons.correction: Increase your economy and tech, strengthen your ground army, and keep scouting to identify the enemy's plan.
lessons.mistake: Over-committing to an attack without knowing the opponent's composition, or neglecting scouting to confirm their greed.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you see the enemy's first combat units or tech structures.
lessons.title: Unknown Enemy: Avoid Overcommitting Without Scouting
lessons.when: Early-midgame, enemy shows heavy economy and tech investment with moderate production; your army is ground-based with Zerglings and Queens.
lessons.why: Matching the enemy's economy and tech is important to avoid falling behind, while maintaining a defensive ground army.
